The chosen independent input variables cover velocity (U_inf), a kinematic diffusion parameter (nu), an integrated quadratic velocity measure (MKE with dimensions L^3 T^-2), and three length scales (delta, delta*, theta). Their dimensional exponents are well-known from fluid mechanics, so the dimensionless output can be formed from nondimensional combinations of these inputs.

variables.physical_definition: Free-stream velocity: mean flow speed far from the boundary layer.
Kinematic viscosity of the fluid (dynamic viscosity divided by density).
Integrated mean-flow kinetic energy: integral from 0 to delta of U(y)^2 dy (U squared integrated across the boundary layer).
Boundary layer thickness (delta): distance from the wall where U reaches 99% of U_inf.
Displacement thickness (delta*): integral measure of the boundary layer representing the deficit in mass flow (∫(1 - U/U_inf) dy).
Momentum thickness (theta): integral measure of momentum deficit in the boundary layer (∫ (U/U_inf)(1 - U/U_inf) dy).
